title: Extension Uplift Where an Earlier Request on the Keyturn Trip Booking Reservation Lapsed or Was Declined
content:
On a Keyturn Trip Booking that has been running for at least 7 days, the extension uplift is set by what has already happened to the earlier extension requests standing against the reservation.

1. Where the reservation carries an extension request that expired without a decision and the trip has run for at least 7 days, the extension uplift is 4 per cent.
2. Where the reservation carries no request that expired without a decision but carries one that was declined, and the trip has run for at least 7 days, the extension uplift is 12 per cent.
3. In every other case the extension uplift is the standard one.

The days the trip has run are counted from the day the trip actually started to the day of handling, the day it started not counted and the day of handling counted.

### The order of the two conditions

| Requests standing against the reservation | Days the trip has run | Extension uplift |
|---|---|---|
| At least one that expired without a decision | 7 or more | 4 per cent |
| None expired, at least one declined | 7 or more | 12 per cent |
| None expired and none declined | 7 or more | The standard one |
| Any | Fewer than 7 | The standard one |

An expired request governs over a declined one: where the reservation carries both, the first row applies and the uplift is 4 per cent. The second row is reached only where no expired request stands at all. Seven days is reached rather than passed.

*Hypothetical.* A trip that has been running 20 days whose reservation carries one request that expired without a decision and two that were declined takes an uplift of 4 per cent. The same reservation with two declined requests and none expired takes 12 per cent. A trip that has been running 3 days takes the standard uplift whatever its requests show.
